requirements.original: They are declared by the `var template` keyword followed by a type identifier and a variable identifier.
requirements.canonical: A template variable declaration IS the `var template` keywords followed by a type identifier and a variable identifier.

improper_terms.proper: `var` keyword followed by a template modifier (TemplateModifier)

ambiguity.issue: The prose speaks of a single 'var template keyword' and only a type identifier, while the syntactical structure uses `var` TemplateModifier (template, possibly with restriction) and TypeOrNestedTypeDef (which also allows a nested type definition or automatic typing).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- They are declared by the `var template` keyword followed by a type identifier and a variable identifier.

requirements.original: An initial content can be assigned at declaration.
requirements.canonical: A template variable declaration MAY assign an initial content to the template variable.

readings: A template variable declaration MAY assign an initial content to the template variable (the assignment is optional).
A template variable declaration SHALL assign an initial content, as the syntactical structure requires ":=" TemplateBody.
ambiguity.issue: The prose suggests an optional initial content, but the syntax block of 11.2 makes ":=" TemplateBody mandatory. The prose reading is kept in the canonical text; test authors should follow the syntax block.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- An initial content can be assigned at declaration.

requirements.original: In addition to values, template variables may also store matching mechanisms (see clause 15.6.6).
requirements.canonical: A template variable MAY store matching mechanisms in addition to values.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- In addition to values, template variables may also store matching mechanisms (see clause 15.6.6).

requirements.original: Template variables may be used on the right hand side as well as on the left hand side of assignments, following the `return` keyword in bodies of functions defining a template-type return value in their headers and may be passed as actual parameters to template-type formal parameters.
requirements.canonical: A template variable MAY be used on the right hand side and on the left hand side of assignments.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- Template variables may be used on the right hand side as well as on the left hand side of assignments, following the `return` keyword in bodies of functions defining a template-type return value in their headers and may be passed as actual parameters to template-type formal parameters.

requirements.original: Template variables may be used on the right hand side as well as on the left hand side of assignments, following the `return` keyword in bodies of functions defining a template-type return value in their headers and may be passed as actual parameters to template-type formal parameters.
requirements.canonical: A template variable MAY be used following the `return` keyword in the body of a function that defines a template-type return value in its header.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- Template variables may be used on the right hand side as well as on the left hand side of assignments, following the `return` keyword in bodies of functions defining a template-type return value in their headers and may be passed as actual parameters to template-type formal parameters.

requirements.original: Template variables may be passed as actual parameters to template-type formal parameters.
requirements.canonical: A template variable MAY be passed as actual parameter to a template-type formal parameter.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- Template variables may be passed as actual parameters to template-type formal parameters.

requirements.original: It is also allowed to assign a template instance to a template variable or a template variable field.
requirements.canonical: A template instance MAY be assigned to a template variable or to a field of a template variable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- It is also allowed to assign a template instance to a template variable or a template variable field.

requirements.original: var TemplateModifier [ (@lazy | @fuzzy) [ @deterministic ] ] [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] { VarIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] ":=" TemplateBody [ "," ] }+ [ ";" ]
requirements.canonical: A template variable declaration has the syntax `var` TemplateModifier [ ( `@lazy` | `@fuzzy` ) [ `@deterministic` ] ] [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] followed by one or more comma-separated VarIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] ":=" TemplateBody and an optional ";".
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- var TemplateModifier [ (@lazy | @fuzzy) [ @deterministic ] ] [ TypeOrNestedTypeDef ] { VarIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] ":=" TemplateBody [ "," ] }+ [ ";" ]

requirements.original: A template variable may change its template during test execution several times.
requirements.canonical: A template variable MAY change its template several times during test execution.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- A template variable may change its template during test execution several times.

requirements.original: A template or value can be assigned several times to a template variable.
requirements.canonical: A template or value MAY be assigned several times to a template variable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- A template or value can be assigned several times to a template variable.

requirements.original: The template variable can be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.canonical: A template variable MAY be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- The template variable can be referenced multiple times in a TTCN-3 module.

requirements.original: The content of a template variable can be restricted to the matching mechanisms specific value and omit in the same way as formal template parameters, see clause 5.4.1.2.
requirements.canonical: The content of a template variable MAY be restricted by a template restriction to the matching mechanisms specific value and `omit`, in the same way as formal template parameters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- The content of a template variable can be restricted to the matching mechanisms specific value and omit in the same way as formal template parameters, see clause 5.4.1.2.

requirements.original: The restriction template (omit) can be replaced by the shorthand notation omit.
requirements.canonical: The template restriction `template (omit)` MAY be replaced by the shorthand notation `omit`.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- The restriction template (omit) can be replaced by the shorthand notation omit.

requirements.original: NOTE 1: String and list type templates can be concatenated, see clause 15.11.
requirements.canonical: A string type template or a list type template CAN be concatenated.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- NOTE 1: String and list type templates can be concatenated, see clause 15.11.

requirements.original: a) Template variables shall not be declared or used in a module definitions part (i.e. global variables are not supported in TTCN-3).
requirements.canonical: A template variable SHALL NOT be declared or used in a module definitions part.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- a) Template variables shall not be declared or used in a module definitions part (i.e. global variables are not supported in TTCN-3).

requirements.original: b) When used on the right hand side of assignments template variables shall not be operands of TTCN-3 operators (see clause 7.1) and the variable on the left hand side shall be a template variable too.
requirements.canonical: A template variable used on the right hand side of an assignment SHALL NOT be an operand of a TTCN-3 operator.
requirements.condition: the template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- b) When used on the right hand side of assignments template variables shall not be operands of TTCN-3 operators (see clause 7.1) and the variable on the left hand side shall be a template variable too.

requirements.original: b) When used on the right hand side of assignments template variables shall not be operands of TTCN-3 operators (see clause 7.1) and the variable on the left hand side shall be a template variable too.
requirements.canonical: If a template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment, the variable on the left hand side SHALL be a template variable.
requirements.condition: the template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment

readings: If a template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment, the variable on the left hand side SHALL be a template variable.

If a template variable is used on the right hand side of an assignment, the target on the left hand side SHALL be a template variable or a field of a template variable (e.g. accessed via dot or index notation).
ambiguity.issue: 'the variable on the left hand side' does not say whether a field or element of a template variable counts; the second reading is consistent with 11.2-s006, the first is the literal reading and is chosen.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- b) When used on the right hand side of assignments template variables shall not be operands of TTCN-3 operators (see clause 7.1) and the variable on the left hand side shall be a template variable too.

requirements.original: c) When accessing element of template variables either on the left hand side or on the right hand side of assignments, the rules given in clause 15.6 shall apply.
requirements.canonical: When an element of a template variable is accessed on the left hand side or the right hand side of an assignment, the rules of clause 15.6 SHALL apply.
requirements.condition: an element of a template variable is accessed in an assignment
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- c) When accessing element of template variables either on the left hand side or on the right hand side of assignments, the rules given in clause 15.6 shall apply.

requirements.original: NOTE 2: While it is not allowed to directly apply TTCN-3 operations to template variables, it is allowed to use the dot notation and the index notation to inspect and modify template variable fields.
requirements.canonical: The dot notation and the index notation MAY be used to inspect and modify fields of a template variable, although TTCN-3 operations SHALL NOT be applied directly to template variables.

ambiguity.issue: The NOTE says 'TTCN-3 operations' while restriction b) it explains speaks of 'TTCN-3 operators (see clause 7.1)'.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- NOTE 2: While it is not allowed to directly apply TTCN-3 operations to template variables, it is allowed to use the dot notation and the index notation to inspect and modify template variable fields.

requirements.original: d) Use of uninitialized template variables at other places than the left hand side of assignments, in return statements, or as actual parameters passed to formal parameters shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: Use of an uninitialized template variable at any place other than the left hand side of an assignment, a return statement, or an actual parameter passed to a formal parameter SHALL cause an error.

readings: Use of an uninitialized template variable in any other place SHALL cause an error (static or dynamic).
Use of an uninitialized template variable in any other place SHALL cause a dynamic error at runtime only.
ambiguity.issue: The kind of error (compile-time or runtime) is not stated; since template variable declarations require an initial TemplateBody, it is also unclear how a template variable can be uninitialized. The generic reading is chosen.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- d) Use of uninitialized template variables at other places than the left hand side of assignments, in return statements, or as actual parameters passed to formal parameters shall cause an error.

requirements.original: f) If the template variable is restricted, then the template used to initialize it shall contain only the matching mechanisms as described in clause 15.8.
requirements.canonical: If a template variable is restricted, the template used to initialize it SHALL contain only the matching mechanisms permitted by the restriction as described in clause 15.8.
requirements.condition: the template variable has a template restriction
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- f) If the template variable is restricted, then the template used to initialize it shall contain only the matching mechanisms as described in clause 15.8.

requirements.original: g) Template variables, similarly to global and local templates, shall be fully specified in order to be used in sending and receiving operations.
requirements.canonical: A template variable SHALL be completely initialized in order to be used in a sending or receiving operation, as global and local templates.
requirements.condition: the template variable is used in a sending or receiving operation

ambiguity.issue: 'fully specified' is not a defined term; the glossary term 'completely initialized' is meant. For sending operations the template additionally has to resolve to a value (clause 15.0).

requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- g) Template variables, similarly to global and local templates, shall be fully specified in order to be used in sending and receiving operations.

requirements.original: h) Restrictions on templates in clause 15.0 shall apply.
requirements.canonical: The restrictions on templates given in clause 15.0 SHALL apply to template variables.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- h) Restrictions on templates in clause 15.0 shall apply.

requirements.original: i) The initialization or assignment of a fuzzy or lazy variable shall not contain function calls of functions with inout or out parameters.
requirements.canonical: The initialization or assignment of a lazy or fuzzy template variable SHALL NOT contain a call of a function with `inout` or `out` parameters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- i) The initialization or assignment of a fuzzy or lazy variable shall not contain function calls of functions with inout or out parameters.

requirements.original: The called functions may use other functions with inout or out parameters internally.
requirements.canonical: A function called in the initialization or assignment of a lazy or fuzzy template variable MAY internally call other functions with `inout` or `out` parameters.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- The called functions may use other functions with inout or out parameters internally.

requirements.original: j) If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the template body assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or the initialization of a global non-fuzzy template), the variable SHALL be declared `@deterministic`.
requirements.condition: a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- j) If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the template body assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.original: j) If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the template body assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.canonical: If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context, the template body assigned to the variable SHALL fulfil the restrictions on the content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.
requirements.condition: a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in a deterministic context
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- j) If a lazy or fuzzy template variable is used in deterministic contexts (i.e. during the evaluation of a snapshot or initialization of global non-fuzzy templates), it shall be declared @deterministic and the template body assigned to the variable shall fulfill the restrictions imposed on content of functions used in special places given in clause 16.1.4.

requirements.original: k) Using the dot notation (see clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.2.1 and 6.2.5.1) and index notation (see clause 6.2.7) for referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value, which actual value is null shall cause an error.
requirements.canonical: Using the dot notation or the index notation to reference a field, alternative or element of an address value whose actual value is `null` SHALL cause an error.
requirements.condition: the actual value of the address value is `null` (in the context of template variables)
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- k) Using the dot notation (see clauses 6.2.1.1, 6.2.2.1 and 6.2.5.1) and index notation (see clause 6.2.7) for referencing a field, alternative or element of an address value, which actual value is null shall cause an error.

requirements.original: l) The template body at the right-hand side of the assignment symbol shall evaluate to a value or template, which is type compatible with the variable being declared.
requirements.canonical: The template body on the right-hand side of the assignment symbol in a template variable declaration SHALL evaluate to a value or template that is type compatible with the declared template variable.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- l) The template body at the right-hand side of the assignment symbol shall evaluate to a value or template, which is type compatible with the variable being declared.

requirements.original: m) The template body at the right-hand side of the assignment symbol shall evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.
requirements.canonical: The template body on the right-hand side of the assignment symbol in a template variable declaration SHALL evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- m) The template body at the right-hand side of the assignment symbol shall evaluate to an object that is at least partially initialized.

requirements.original: n) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" TemplateBody) shall be present.
requirements.canonical: If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a template variable declaration, the ArrayDef part SHALL be missing as well.
requirements.condition: the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- n) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" TemplateBody) shall be present.

requirements.original: n) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" TemplateBody) shall be present.
requirements.canonical: If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from a template variable declaration, the assignment part (":=" TemplateBody) SHALL be present.
requirements.condition: the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- n) If the TypeOrNestedTypeDef part is missing from the declaration, the ArrayDef part shall be missing as well and the assignment part (i.e. ":=" TemplateBody) shall be present.

requirements.original: var template @fuzzy float v_fuzzTemp1 := rnd(); // evaluated on every usage
requirements.canonical: A fuzzy template variable IS evaluated on every usage.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 11.2 -- var template @fuzzy float v_fuzzTemp1 := rnd(); // evaluated on every usage

requirements.original: Timers can be declared and used in test cases, functions and altsteps.
requirements.canonical: A timer MAY be declared and used in a test case, a function or an altstep.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- Timers can be declared and used in test cases, functions and altsteps.

requirements.original: Additionally, timers can be declared in component type definitions.
requirements.canonical: A timer MAY be declared in a component type definition.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- Additionally, timers can be declared in component type definitions.

requirements.original: These timers can be used in test cases, functions and altsteps which are running on the given component type.
requirements.canonical: A timer declared in a component type definition MAY be used in a test case, function or altstep that runs on that component type.
requirements.condition: the test case, function or altstep has a runs on clause referencing the component type

readings: A component timer MAY be used in a test case, function or altstep whose runs on clause references the component type.
A component timer MAY be used in a test case, function or altstep whose runs on clause references the component type or a type compatible with it (e.g. an extending component type).
ambiguity.issue: 'running on the given component type' does not say whether compatible (extended) component types are included; chose the literal reading.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- These timers can be used in test cases, functions and altsteps which are running on the given component type.

requirements.original: A timer declaration may have an optional default duration value assigned to it.
requirements.canonical: A timer declaration MAY assign a default duration value to the timer.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- A timer declaration may have an optional default duration value assigned to it.

requirements.original: The timer shall be started with this value if no other value is specified.
requirements.canonical: When a timer is started without a specified timer value, the timer SHALL be started with its default duration value.
requirements.condition: no other value is specified at start
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- The timer shall be started with this value if no other value is specified.

requirements.original: The timer value shall be a non-negative float value (i.e. greater than or equal to 0.0) where the base unit is seconds.
requirements.canonical: A timer value SHALL be a non-negative `float` value (greater than or equal to 0.0).

readings: A default duration value in a timer declaration SHALL be a non-negative float value.
Any timer value (default duration or value given in a start operation) SHALL be a non-negative float value.
ambiguity.issue: 'The timer value' follows the default duration sentences; chose the general reading that covers all timer values.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- The timer value shall be a non-negative float value (i.e. greater than or equal to 0.0) where the base unit is seconds.

requirements.original: The timer value shall be a non-negative float value (i.e. greater than or equal to 0.0) where the base unit is seconds.
requirements.canonical: The base unit of a timer value IS seconds.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- The timer value shall be a non-negative float value (i.e. greater than or equal to 0.0) where the base unit is seconds.

requirements.original: In addition to single timer instances, timer arrays can also be declared.
requirements.canonical: A timer array MAY be declared.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- In addition to single timer instances, timer arrays can also be declared.

requirements.original: Default duration(s) of the elements of a timer array shall be assigned using a value array.
requirements.canonical: The default durations of the elements of a timer array SHALL be assigned using a value array.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- Default duration(s) of the elements of a timer array shall be assigned using a value array.

requirements.original: Default duration(s) assignment shall use the array value notation as specified in clause 15.8.2.
requirements.canonical: A default duration assignment of a timer array SHALL use the array value notation.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- Default duration(s) assignment shall use the array value notation as specified in clause 15.8.2.

requirements.original: If the default duration assignment is wished to be skipped for some element(s) of the timer array, it shall explicitly be declared by using the not used symbol ("-").
requirements.canonical: If the default duration of an element of a timer array is to be skipped, the element SHALL be explicitly marked with the not used symbol ("-") in the default duration value array.
requirements.condition: no default duration is wished for some element(s) of the timer array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- If the default duration assignment is wished to be skipped for some element(s) of the timer array, it shall explicitly be declared by using the not used symbol ("-").

requirements.original: timer { TimerIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] ":=" TimerValue [ "," ] } [ ";" ]
requirements.canonical: A timer declaration has the syntax `timer` followed by one or more TimerIdentifier [ArrayDef] ":=" TimerValue items separated by optional commas, optionally terminated by ";".

readings: The ":=" TimerValue part of a timer declaration IS mandatory, as written in the syntactical structure.
The ":=" TimerValue part of a timer declaration IS optional, as stated in the prose (s005) and shown in EXAMPLE 1 (t_myTimer2).
ambiguity.issue: The syntactical structure shows the default value assignment as mandatory, contradicting the prose and example; the optional reading is the intended one.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- timer { TimerIdentifier [ ArrayDef ] ":=" TimerValue [ "," ] } [ ";" ]

requirements.original: Timers are local to components.
requirements.canonical: A timer IS local to a component.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- Timers are local to components.

requirements.original: A component can start and stop a timer, check if a timer is running, read the elapsed time of a running timer and process timeout events after timer expiration.
requirements.canonical: A component CAN start a timer, stop a timer, check whether a timer is running, read the elapsed time of a running timer and process timeout events after timer expiration.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- A component can start and stop a timer, check if a timer is running, read the elapsed time of a running timer and process timeout events after timer expiration.

requirements.original: The timer value is interpreted with a base unit of seconds.
requirements.canonical: A timer value IS interpreted with a base unit of seconds.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- The timer value is interpreted with a base unit of seconds.

requirements.original: A timer declared and started in scope units such as functions ceases to exist when the scope unit is left unless there is a constant, variable or parameter defined in the current or higher scope unit or in an activated altstep that contains a reference to it.
requirements.canonical: A timer declared and started in a scope unit (e.g. a function) ceases to exist when the scope unit is left, unless a constant, variable or parameter of the current or a higher scope unit or of an activated altstep contains a reference to the timer.
requirements.condition: the scope unit is left

ambiguity.issue: 'parameter' is used where a formal parameter holding a timer reference is meant.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- A timer declared and started in scope units such as functions ceases to exist when the scope unit is left unless there is a constant, variable or parameter defined in the current or higher scope unit or in an activated altstep that contains a reference to it.

requirements.original: In this case, the timer is kept as long as at least one constant, variable or parameter of the current or higher scope unit or an activated altstep contain a reference to it.
requirements.canonical: A timer declared in a left scope unit IS kept in existence as long as at least one constant, variable or parameter of the current or a higher scope unit or an activated altstep contains a reference to the timer.
requirements.condition: a reference to the timer is held by a constant, variable or parameter of the current or higher scope unit or an activated altstep
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- In this case, the timer is kept as long as at least one constant, variable or parameter of the current or higher scope unit or an activated altstep contain a reference to it.

requirements.original: If a timer ceases to exist, it stops running, will never timeout and cannot be referenced via the any timer or all timer constructs.
requirements.canonical: A timer that ceased to exist stops running.
requirements.condition: the timer ceases to exist
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- If a timer ceases to exist, it stops running, will never timeout and cannot be referenced via the any timer or all timer constructs.

requirements.original: If a timer ceases to exist, it stops running, will never timeout and cannot be referenced via the any timer or all timer constructs.
requirements.canonical: A timer that ceased to exist IS NOT able to time out.
requirements.condition: the timer ceases to exist
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- If a timer ceases to exist, it stops running, will never timeout and cannot be referenced via the any timer or all timer constructs.

requirements.original: If a timer ceases to exist, it stops running, will never timeout and cannot be referenced via the any timer or all timer constructs.
requirements.canonical: A timer that ceased to exist CANNOT be referenced via the `any timer` or `all timer` constructs.
requirements.condition: the timer ceases to exist
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- If a timer ceases to exist, it stops running, will never timeout and cannot be referenced via the any timer or all timer constructs.

requirements.original: If not stated otherwise, timers have the same semantics as constants of a timer type.
requirements.canonical: Unless stated otherwise, a timer IS semantically equivalent to a constant of a timer type.
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- If not stated otherwise, timers have the same semantics as constants of a timer type.

requirements.original: a) In case of a single timer, the default duration value shall resolve to a non-negative numerical float value (i.e. the value shall be greater or equal 0.0, infinity and not_a_number are disallowed).
requirements.canonical: The default duration value of a single timer SHALL resolve to a non-negative numerical `float` value (greater than or equal to 0.0).
requirements.condition: single timer
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- a) In case of a single timer, the default duration value shall resolve to a non-negative numerical float value (i.e. the value shall be greater or equal 0.0, infinity and not_a_number are disallowed).

requirements.original: a) In case of a single timer, the default duration value shall resolve to a non-negative numerical float value (i.e. the value shall be greater or equal 0.0, infinity and not_a_number are disallowed).
requirements.canonical: The default duration value of a single timer SHALL NOT be `infinity` or `not_a_number`.
requirements.condition: single timer
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- a) In case of a single timer, the default duration value shall resolve to a non-negative numerical float value (i.e. the value shall be greater or equal 0.0, infinity and not_a_number are disallowed).

requirements.original: b) In case of a timer array, it shall resolve to an array of float values obeying to restriction a) above of the same size as the size of the timer array.
requirements.canonical: The default duration value of a timer array SHALL resolve to an array of non-negative numerical `float` values (not `infinity` or `not_a_number`).
requirements.condition: timer array

readings: Every element of the default duration array of a timer array SHALL be a non-negative numerical float value.
Every element of the default duration array that is not the not used symbol SHALL be a non-negative numerical float value.
ambiguity.issue: Restriction b) does not mention elements skipped with "-" (allowed by s011); chose the reading that excludes skipped elements implicitly.

requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- b) In case of a timer array, it shall resolve to an array of float values obeying to restriction a) above of the same size as the size of the timer array.

requirements.original: b) In case of a timer array, it shall resolve to an array of float values obeying to restriction a) above of the same size as the size of the timer array.
requirements.canonical: The default duration array of a timer array SHALL have the same size as the timer array.
requirements.condition: timer array
requirements.header: // @requirement: 12 -- b) In case of a timer array, it shall resolve to an array of float values obeying to restriction a) above of the same size as the size of the timer array.
